title: Headless rocGDB functional debugging for rocKE kernels
description: Develop a non-interactive functional-debugging path for optimized rocKE kernels. Preserve source names, types, lane state, and machine locations without adding kernel printf calls or changing executable instructions. This epic records the 2026-08-17 feasibility experiments and the remaining compiler, debugger, rendering, and integration work.
notes: Operational handoff, 2026-08-17: Work is in the isolated worktree branch users/mpodkory/rocke/headless-debug-values. The primary checkout was not modified. The prototype has two local checkpoint commits and has not been pushed or otherwise published; do not publish without explicit authorization. The first checkpoint covers IRBuilder.debug_value, matching Python and C++ LLVM selected-value emission, universal GEMM tid selection, focused debug-info tests, the physical-register decoder, and its tests. The second checkpoint closes rocke-wdl.7: it adds LayoutMap-derived semantic manifests, a manifest generator for existing MMA roles, and the rocke value command with logical dtype and packed storage decoding, multi-register collections, lane activity, machine locations, explicit availability states, layout-aware tile reconstruction, human output, and deterministic JSONL. Local experiment checkpoints, generated LLVM/object/HSACO evidence, build trees, and the prototype virtual environment are outside the repository and must not be committed. Load the ubuntu-24 and rocm-nightly modules for current validation. Rebuild native code only through Slurm using --constraint=MARKHAM,CPUONLY. Run GPU and rocGDB validation through Slurm using --constraint=MARKHAM,GFX942. Initial selected-value validation passed the focused Python and native C++ suites, the 68-family differential gate, LLVM DWARF verification, executable-text identity, numeric verification, and batch rocGDB name lookup. Structured-renderer validation passed 72 Python tests with 5 skips, 4 object-code tests deliberately deselected on the login node, and 4 subtests; Black and Ruff passed; a batch rocGDB run with the 2026-08-17 nightly read four VGPRs across 64 lanes, reconstructed a 16x16 MFMA coordinate space, emitted one structured JSON record, and exited normally. That live layout probe validated transport and reconstruction with explicit physical expressions; it did not claim those registers semantically held an accumulator at the stopped PC. Automatic DWARF vector-location resolution is rocke-wdl.10, the next functional milestone. O0 and the scratch LLVM patch remain out of scope. rocke-wdl.9 remains a separate lower-priority runtime-packaging investigation.

title: Compare kernel printf, rocGDB stops, and ATT for debugging
description: Recorded the observation semantics of device printf, debugger register inspection, and ATT traces. Device printf and debugger stops can perturb scheduling and synchronization behavior. ATT is the preferred evidence source for synchronization and ordering defects; debugger inspection remains useful for functional state.

title: Connect DWARF vector locations to structured logical values
description: Remove the manual physical-expression step for selected fragment values. Extend selected-value metadata to supported vectors, associate semantic manifests with the selected source value, consume the DWARF location valid at the stopped PC, and feed the resolved register pieces into the structured renderer. Preserve explicit optimized-out and unavailable-location states. Verify unchanged executable text and one known accumulator reconstruction against an independent result.

title: Prototype deterministic rocGDB register decoding
description: Implemented a headless rocGDB command that decodes per-lane register values as human-readable tables or deterministic JSONL. Covered f32, packed f16 and bf16, OCP and FNUZ float8 encodings, EXEC activity, lane selection, and active-lane filtering. Unit tests, formatting checks, and a batch rocGDB run on a Slurm gfx942 node passed.

title: Prove named logical-value DWARF at O0 without ISA changes
description: Added scratch-only llvm.dbg.value metadata for tid in an existing universal GEMM. LLVM emitted a typed source variable and a PC-specific VGPR location; rocGDB printed tid by name. Baseline and annotated text sections were identical and numeric verification passed. Boundary: the object used O0, while normal rocKE COMGR compilation uses O3.

title: Investigate selected logical-value loss in the production O3 pipeline
description: Normal rocKE COMGR compilation uses O3. With the same tid annotation used by the O0 feasibility experiment, late O3 MIR contains DBG_VALUE noreg before the O0 VGPR-to-AGPR case occurs. Find the first pass that loses the location and determine whether the value is truly unavailable or debug tracking is incomplete. Any production design must be validated at O3.
notes: Clean unmodified nightly LLVM 23 O3 validation found no early location loss. tid remained an instruction reference to VGPR0 through code generation; LiveDebugValues emitted a VGPR0 location; linked HSACO range was [0x1818,0x1878). Annotated and baseline O3 text sections were identical. Numeric verification and batch rocGDB print-by-name inside the range passed.
close_reason: Completed: the suspected O3 location-loss premise was disproved by an end-to-end run with unmodified LLVM. The bounded scalar path works at production O3.

title: Report the O0 AMDGPU VGPR-to-AGPR LiveDebugValues gap upstream
description: At O0, MIR before and after LiveDebugValues leaves DBG_VALUE in a VGPR even though V_ACCVGPR_WRITE_B32_e64 copies the value to AGPR0. AMDGPU does not classify accumulator reads or writes as copy-like for debug propagation. Prepare a minimal LLVM reproducer and determine whether copy-like tracking is sound under EXEC masking and divergent control flow before proposing an upstream fix.
close_reason: Out of scope for this prototype: rocKE production compilation uses O3, and O0 debug-location support is not a practical requirement.

title: Verify rocGDB consumption of AGPR DWARF locations
description: AMDGPU assigns DWARF register numbers to AGPRs, but end-to-end rocGDB consumption has not been proven. Produce or construct an AGPR location, select representative waves and lanes, and verify register access, lane interpretation, and behavior for inactive lanes.
close_reason: Out of scope for the prototype: AGPR location consumption was only needed for the discarded O0 VGPR-to-AGPR path.

title: Add structured headless rendering for logical dtypes, tiles, and layouts
description: Extend the register decoder into a non-interactive functional-debugging interface. Preserve source name, dtype, lane activity, machine location, and explicit availability status. Add rendering for packed floating-point types, collections, tiles, and layout-aware reconstruction while keeping deterministic JSONL for agents.
notes: Implemented a portable rocke-debug-manifest/v1 exporter that evaluates existing LayoutMap objects with integer inputs, so debugger code does not duplicate MMA layout formulas. Added a manifest generator for ArchTarget MMA roles with explicit physical expressions. Added the rocke value rocGDB command with logical dtype and storage dtype separation, multi-register and packed-element collections, layout-aware tile reconstruction, human output, strict deterministic JSONL, lane activity, machine-location provenance, and explicit unavailable states. Validation: 72 Python tests passed, 5 skipped, 4 object-code tests deliberately deselected on the login node, and 4 subtests passed. Black and Ruff passed. A batch rocGDB run with the 2026-08-17 ROCm nightly on gfx942 read four VGPRs across 64 lanes, reconstructed a 16x16 MFMA coordinate space, emitted one structured JSON record, and exited normally. The physical expressions in that integration probe were explicit and were not claimed to be a semantic accumulator location at the stopped PC. Automatic DWARF location discovery remains separate follow-up work.
close_reason: Structured manifest generation, logical collection and tile rendering, explicit statuses, and live batch rocGDB integration are complete.

title: Design dual-emitter metadata for selected rocKE logical values
description: Define an opt-in representation for selected logical values that both Python and C++ rocKE emitters lower identically. Preserve source name, type, and semantic fragment information without artificial uses or executable-code changes. Do not implement until the O3 compiler behavior and debugger location contract are understood.
notes: Implemented the bounded scalar selected-value path in the isolated prototype. IRBuilder.debug_value is a no-op without source capture and records name, SSA value, type, and source stack when enabled. Python and C++ LLVM emitters produce byte-identical FullDebug, DIBasicType, DILocalVariable, and llvm.dbg.value metadata for llvm20, llvm22, and llvm23. The variable is scoped to the innermost source subprogram; retainedNodes is intentionally omitted after LLVM rejected invalid cross-subprogram ownership. Validation: source-focused suite 48 passed with 3 flavor subtests; native C++ build and 5 CTests passed on Slurm MARKHAM,CPUONLY; full 68-family LLVM-IR differential gate green; LLVM 23 DWARF verification green; normal, line-table, and selected O3 text byte-identical; universal GEMM numeric verification passed; batch rocGDB printed tid as i32 value 0 at PC 0x1818.
close_reason: Bounded scalar dual-emitter implementation and end-to-end validation complete.

title: Resolve rocKE runtime integration with multi-arch nightly wheels
description: The multi-arch nightly wheel layout places HIP and COMGR libraries under the ROCm SDK core package rather than the older torch lib location. Explicit library selection removed resolver ambiguity, but the generated code object still failed to load under the wheel runtime. Treat this as a runtime integration issue separate from rocGDB functionality.
